name: cato-honey-cheesecake-recipe
description: A Roman statesman's farming handbook set down a baked cheese-and-flour cake finished with a coating of honey.

name: indian-sugar-crystallisation
description: Sugar makers in northern India learned to boil cane juice into hard crystals that could be stored and traded.

name: gingerbread-reaches-europe
description: An Armenian monk is traditionally said to have taught French bakers to make spiced ginger bread.

name: nuremberg-lebkuchen-recorded
description: Bakers in a Franconian trading city were documented making honey-and-spice gingerbread, later a Christmas market staple.

name: candy-cane-first-handed-out
friendly_name: The Candy Cane Is Handed Out
description: A German choirmaster is said to have bent white sugar sticks into shepherd's crooks to keep children quiet in church.

name: cafe-procope-gelato
description: A Sicilian entrepreneur's Left Bank coffeehouse popularised flavoured iced cream among Parisians.

name: bakers-chocolate-founded
description: An Irish immigrant and a Boston doctor began grinding cocoa beans at a mill, founding a long-lived American chocolate maker.

name: turkish-delight-on-sale
description: A confectioner opened a sweet shop in Istanbul selling soft starch-and-sugar jellies that became famous across Europe.

name: sachertorte-invented
description: A teenage apprentice improvised a dense chocolate sponge with apricot jam for a prince's guests in Vienna.

name: cadbury-chocolate-box
description: Richard Cadbury packed bonbons into decorated boxes, turning chocolate into a gift for sweethearts.

name: fry-chocolate-easter-egg
description: An English chocolate firm made hollow eggs from smooth moulded chocolate to give at the spring holiday.

name: cracker-jack-debuts

description: A Chicago popcorn vendor sold molasses-coated popcorn and peanuts to crowds at a world's fair.

name: jell-o-sold-as-dessert
friendly_name: Jell-O Is Sold as a Dessert
description: A New York cough-syrup maker named a fruit-flavoured gelatin powder, which a firm soon marketed to home cooks.

name: hersheys-milk-chocolate-bar
description: A Pennsylvania caramel maker launched an affordable milk chocolate bar for the American mass market.

name: oreo-introduced
description: The National Biscuit Company launched a cream-filled chocolate sandwich cookie that became the best-selling in the world.

name: eskimo-pie-patented
description: An Iowa shopkeeper coated ice cream bars in chocolate, creating a hand-held ice cream treat sold nationally.

name: haribo-gummy-bear
description: A Bonn confectioner poured fruit-flavoured gelatin into bear-shaped moulds, called the dancing bear at first.

name: pavlova-created

name: mars-bar-launched

name: kit-kat-launched

name: chupa-chups-lollipop
description: A Spanish confectioner put a stick in a hard candy so children could eat it without sticky fingers.

name: nutella-launched
description: An Italian firm branded its hazelnut-and-cocoa spread, grown from a wartime stretching of scarce chocolate.

name: cadbury-creme-egg-named
description: Cadbury renamed its fondant-filled chocolate egg, which became the spring treat sold by the hundreds of millions.

name: kinder-surprise-launched
description: An Italian confectioner hid a plastic toy inside a hollow chocolate egg for children to find.

name: ben-jerrys-scoop-shop
friendly_name: Ben and Jerry Open Their Scoop Shop
description: Two friends sold hand-made ice cream from a renovated Vermont petrol station, starting a famous brand.

name: cronut-hits-new-york
description: A SoHo pastry chef fried laminated dough in a doughnut shape, producing queues around the block.
